learningObjective: Choose where billable-mass calculation belongs when callers must share one result derived from shipment measures and carrier class.

question.prompt: A parcel quote has 3 measured dimensions and a carrier class divisor. The quoted billable mass is used by two callers; neither caller owns measurement rules. Choose where billable-mass calculation belongs when callers must share one result derived from shipment measures and carrier class.

options.text: Place a calculation with the cohesive information it needs, rather than duplicating it in callers.
Let the ParcelQuote calculate billable mass from its dimensions and selected carrier class.
A second caller can use a different rounding or divisor rule, so identical parcel state can yield conflicting quotes.

feedback.reason: Choose where billable-mass calculation belongs when callers must share one result derived from shipment measures and carrier class. The saved number can drift from the measures after an amendment.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The saved number can drift from the measures after an amendment.
details.scenarioApplication: ParcelQuote owns both the measures and carrier-class choice used by this derived value.
details.errorCorrection: Have each checkout caller calculate billable mass from the exposed dimensions. Store billable mass as an independently editable field beside the dimensions.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Both callers now obtain the same quote calculation from the object that has all required inputs.
details.transfer: If carrier policy becomes independently versioned, inject a policy value; do not duplicate the arithmetic in each caller.

messages.text: Have each checkout caller calculate billable mass from the exposed dimensions.
Store billable mass as an independently editable field beside the dimensions.

learningObjective: Choose how the session should report remaining places when confirmation status changes.

question.prompt: A workshop session stores confirmed attendee IDs and has a visible capacity. Waitlisted people are not confirmed. Choose how the session should report remaining places when confirmation status changes.

options.text: Have WorkshopSession compute remaining places from its confirmed attendee set and capacity.
A cancellation path can update membership but miss the counter, so the displayed number no longer describes the stored attendees.
Derive a summary from the authoritative membership state it describes.

feedback.reason: Choose how the session should report remaining places when confirmation status changes. That count includes people who do not consume a confirmed place under the stated rule.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That count includes people who do not consume a confirmed place under the stated rule.
details.scenarioApplication: The session already owns both capacity and confirmed membership.
details.errorCorrection: Maintain a separate remainingPlaces counter that each registration caller increments or decrements. Ask the dashboard to count every attendee record, including waitlisted people.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Remaining capacity changes whenever a person becomes or ceases to be confirmed.
details.transfer: A reporting projection may cache the result, but its source must remain this confirmed-membership rule.

messages.text: Maintain a separate remainingPlaces counter that each registration caller increments or decrements.
Ask the dashboard to count every attendee record, including waitlisted people.

learningObjective: Choose how an issued line should calculate its amount after catalog prices change.

question.prompt: An invoice line captures quantity and unit price at issue time. The catalog price may later change; old invoices must still show the issued amount. Choose how an issued line should calculate its amount after catalog prices change.

options.text: That substitutes current catalog state for the values the issued line captured.
Keep historical behavior cohesive with the state captured by the historical object.
Let InvoiceLine compute its amount from its captured quantity and unit price.

feedback.reason: Choose how an issued line should calculate its amount after catalog prices change. The same issued line can then display different totals depending on which screen recalculated it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The same issued line can then display different totals depending on which screen recalculated it.
details.scenarioApplication: InvoiceLine has the exact captured values that define this historical amount.
details.errorCorrection: Re-read today’s catalog price whenever an old invoice is displayed. Copy the invoice amount into every screen-specific presenter and treat each copy as authoritative.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Catalog edits affect future lines while the old line continues to show its issued amount.
details.transfer: A tax policy can remain an explicit collaborator if the invoice also captures the applicable policy version.

messages.text: Copy the invoice amount into every screen-specific presenter and treat each copy as authoritative.
Re-read today’s catalog price whenever an old invoice is displayed.

learningObjective: Choose where scaling belongs so one batch can change without altering the master recipe.

question.prompt: A recipe batch stores ingredient quantities for its selected serving count. The master recipe remains unchanged when a cook scales one batch. Choose where scaling belongs so one batch can change without altering the master recipe.

options.text: Distinguish batch-specific state from its source definition when assigning behavior.
Let RecipeBatch calculate its ingredient quantities from its own serving count and the selected recipe revision.
That edits the reusable definition when only one prepared batch is changing.

feedback.reason: Choose where scaling belongs so one batch can change without altering the master recipe. Different consumers can apply different rounding and forget batch-specific adjustments.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Different consumers can apply different rounding and forget batch-specific adjustments.
details.scenarioApplication: The batch owns the chosen serving count and selected source revision.
details.errorCorrection: Let the recipe editor overwrite master quantities each time a cook changes serving count. Let each shopping-list screen independently multiply the master values by the requested servings.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A second batch can scale independently while both retain the same master recipe.
details.transfer: If a recipe revision changes, use its explicit revision rather than mutating batches already prepared from an earlier one.

messages.text: Let the recipe editor overwrite master quantities each time a cook changes serving count.
Let each shopping-list screen independently multiply the master values by the requested servings.

learningObjective: Choose how the playlist should expose its total runtime when tracks are reordered or replaced.

question.prompt: A playlist stores an ordered set of tracks. Track durations come from the playlist’s selected track versions; duration is not manually editable. Choose how the playlist should expose its total runtime when tracks are reordered or replaced.

options.text: Have Playlist compute runtime from its ordered selected track versions.
A track replacement can leave that independent field inconsistent with the actual list.
Keep an aggregate derived from owned members aligned with their ordering and versions.

feedback.reason: Choose how the playlist should expose its total runtime when tracks are reordered or replaced. The playlist’s displayed runtime can depend on unrelated cache freshness instead of its selected members.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The playlist’s displayed runtime can depend on unrelated cache freshness instead of its selected members.
details.scenarioApplication: The playlist owns the ordered membership and selected versions used by the total.
details.errorCorrection: Persist a second editable runtime field and update it from each reorder screen. Have each playback screen sum whichever current track versions its own cache returns.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A reorder or replacement immediately changes the derived runtime through the same rule.
details.transfer: A separately materialized search index may lag, but it should be labeled as a projection rather than the playlist’s authoritative runtime.

messages.text: Persist a second editable runtime field and update it from each reorder screen.
Have each playback screen sum whichever current track versions its own cache returns.

learningObjective: Choose how a historical corrected value should be obtained after the device is recalibrated.

question.prompt: A sensor reading stores the raw measurement and the calibration revision used when it was taken. Later recalibration must not rewrite historical readings. Choose how a historical corrected value should be obtained after the device is recalibrated.

options.text: That reinterprets an old measurement using state that did not apply when it was captured.
Keep historical interpretation tied to the measurement’s captured calibration state.
Have SensorReading apply its captured calibration revision to its raw measurement.

feedback.reason: Choose how a historical corrected value should be obtained after the device is recalibrated. Independent formulas can disagree about the same archived reading.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Independent formulas can disagree about the same archived reading.
details.scenarioApplication: The reading owns the raw value and the calibration revision that gives it historical meaning.
details.errorCorrection: Apply whichever calibration is currently active whenever any screen opens the old reading. Let the chart and export each maintain their own corrected-value formula.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Recalibration changes future readings while archived readings retain their prior interpretation.
details.transfer: If policy requires restating history, model that as an explicit restatement instead of silently changing display behavior.

messages.text: Let the chart and export each maintain their own corrected-value formula.
Apply whichever calibration is currently active whenever any screen opens the old reading.

learningObjective: Choose how the allowance should expose its remaining accepted balance.

question.prompt: A monthly allowance stores a period limit and accepted charges for that period. Draft charges do not reduce available balance. Choose how the allowance should expose its remaining accepted balance.

options.text: Calculate a balance from the exact set of state that counts toward it.
Let MonthlyAllowance subtract its accepted charges from its period limit.
A rejected draft could reduce the balance despite not being part of accepted charges.

feedback.reason: Choose how the allowance should expose its remaining accepted balance. The display would include records excluded by the allowance’s stated accounting state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The display would include records excluded by the allowance’s stated accounting state.
details.scenarioApplication: The allowance owns the period limit and the accepted-charge membership.
details.errorCorrection: Keep a cached balance that every charge editor changes before the charge is accepted. Have each account page subtract all visible charges, including drafts.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Accepting or reversing a charge changes the balance through the same domain rule.
details.transfer: A ledger may independently record accounting entries, but the allowance balance must use the defined accepted set.

messages.text: Keep a cached balance that every charge editor changes before the charge is accepted.
Have each account page subtract all visible charges, including drafts.

learningObjective: Choose how bounds validation should stay consistent across preview and export.

question.prompt: A crop stores an image size and a rectangle. A crop must remain inside the image; the editor previews the same rectangle that export uses. Choose how bounds validation should stay consistent across preview and export.

options.text: Have ImageCrop validate a proposed rectangle against its stored image dimensions.
The two paths can disagree because only one protects the stated geometry.
Place a state-dependent validity check with the object whose dimensions define validity.

feedback.reason: Choose how bounds validation should stay consistent across preview and export. The object can persist an invalid crop before that later render occurs.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The object can persist an invalid crop before that later render occurs.
details.scenarioApplication: ImageCrop has both the rectangle and the image dimensions needed for the check.
details.errorCorrection: Let the preview component check bounds while export accepts any rectangle it receives. Allow callers to mutate rectangle coordinates directly and repair them on the next render.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Both preview and export can use the same valid crop state.
details.transfer: A separate image decoder may validate file format, but it does not replace this geometric check.

messages.text: Let the preview component check bounds while export accepts any rectangle it receives.
Allow callers to mutate rectangle coordinates directly and repair them on the next render.

learningObjective: Choose how meeting duration should be calculated for attendees in different zones.

question.prompt: A meeting stores start and end instants. Each attendee sees those instants in their own time zone; the event does not store a single local wall-clock label. Choose how meeting duration should be calculated for attendees in different zones.

options.text: Across a daylight-saving transition, the displayed wall-clock difference may not equal elapsed time.
Keep duration based on the time representation the event actually owns.
Have Meeting calculate elapsed duration from its stored start and end instants.

feedback.reason: Choose how meeting duration should be calculated for attendees in different zones. That number can contradict the actual interval represented by the event.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That number can contradict the actual interval represented by the event.
details.scenarioApplication: Meeting owns the two instants that define its elapsed duration.
details.errorCorrection: Subtract each attendee’s locally formatted clock labels in the display layer. Store a separate duration that organizers can edit independently of both instants.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Attendees can format those same endpoints locally without changing the underlying duration.
details.transfer: If the product asks for scheduled wall-clock hours, model that separate business quantity explicitly.

messages.text: Store a separate duration that organizers can edit independently of both instants.
Subtract each attendee’s locally formatted clock labels in the display layer.

learningObjective: Choose how the stay should report its number of nights.

question.prompt: A hotel stay stores check-in and check-out calendar dates in the hotel’s local calendar. A stay crossing midnight counts each occupied night; time-zone conversion is not part of this contract. Choose how the stay should report its number of nights.

options.text: Calculate a domain quantity from the dates and counting rule the stay owns.
Have HotelStay count the hotel-local dates from check-in up to but not including check-out.
The prompt defines hotel-local calendar nights, not elapsed 24-hour periods.

feedback.reason: Choose how the stay should report its number of nights. The same stay could then show different night counts on different pages.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The same stay could then show different night counts on different pages.
details.scenarioApplication: HotelStay owns the local dates and the rule that defines an occupied night.
details.errorCorrection: Convert both dates to the traveler’s device zone and subtract elapsed hours divided by 24. Let each booking page decide whether check-out day is inclusive.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The count stays stable when a traveler views the booking from another time zone.
details.transfer: If a business adopts a different date-counting rule, represent that policy explicitly rather than hiding it in a screen.

messages.text: Convert both dates to the traveler’s device zone and subtract elapsed hours divided by 24.
Let each booking page decide whether check-out day is inclusive.

learningObjective: Choose how boundary membership should be evaluated consistently wherever bands are used.

question.prompt: A temperature band has inclusive lower and upper bounds. A reading belongs to the band when it is equal to either endpoint or between them. Choose how boundary membership should be evaluated consistently wherever bands are used.

options.text: Have TemperatureBand answer whether a reading is within its inclusive bounds.
A screen can accidentally omit equality at one endpoint, creating a different band rule.
Keep a value-object predicate with the bounds and endpoint rule it represents.

feedback.reason: Choose how boundary membership should be evaluated consistently wherever bands are used. Membership then depends on stale derived state rather than the selected band.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Membership then depends on stale derived state rather than the selected band.
details.scenarioApplication: TemperatureBand owns the endpoints and inclusive comparison rule.
details.errorCorrection: Let each alert screen compare the reading against the two endpoints itself. Store an isInside flag on each reading and update it whenever any band changes.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Alerting and reporting callers ask the same band about a reading.
details.transfer: If different alert policies require different thresholds, each band instance should carry its own stated bounds.

messages.text: Let each alert screen compare the reading against the two endpoints itself.
Store an isInside flag on each reading and update it whenever any band changes.

learningObjective: Choose how the board should determine the number of ready tasks after a dependency is edited.

question.prompt: A project board stores tasks and dependency links. A task is ready only when all its recorded prerequisites are complete; the board can change links. Choose how the board should determine the number of ready tasks after a dependency is edited.

options.text: A task cannot determine whether other recorded prerequisites are complete from its status alone.
Keep a graph-derived decision with the aggregate that owns the graph being evaluated.
Have ProjectBoard evaluate readiness from its current tasks and dependency links.

feedback.reason: Choose how the board should determine the number of ready tasks after a dependency is edited. That copy can disagree with the board after a link edit.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That copy can disagree with the board after a link edit.
details.scenarioApplication: ProjectBoard owns the collection and links whose combined state determines readiness.
details.errorCorrection: Let every task mark itself ready based only on its own status. Have the dashboard keep its own dependency graph copy and compute readiness there.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A link edit is reflected in the next readiness calculation without asking each task to guess about the graph.
details.transfer: For very large graphs, a computed index may help, but it must be derived from the authoritative board graph.

messages.text: Have the dashboard keep its own dependency graph copy and compute readiness there.
Let every task mark itself ready based only on its own status.

learningObjective: Choose how the risk band should stay aligned with reviewer edits to severity and likelihood.

question.prompt: An inspection finding stores severity and likelihood. The published risk band is the cell in a fixed matrix selected by those two values; reviewers cannot edit the band separately. Choose how the risk band should stay aligned with reviewer edits to severity and likelihood.

options.text: Derive a classification from the attributes that determine it.
Have InspectionFinding select its risk band from its severity, likelihood, and the fixed matrix.
The label can describe a different pair of inputs from the saved finding.

feedback.reason: Choose how the risk band should stay aligned with reviewer edits to severity and likelihood. Reports can classify the same finding differently even though the matrix is fixed by the prompt.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Reports can classify the same finding differently even though the matrix is fixed by the prompt.
details.scenarioApplication: The finding owns the two inputs and the matrix rule defines their classification.
details.errorCorrection: Let reviewers edit a risk label independently after changing severity. Have each report apply its own copy of the severity matrix.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A severity or likelihood correction automatically changes the computed band.
details.transfer: If the matrix itself becomes versioned, capture the matrix revision with the finding.

messages.text: Let reviewers edit a risk label independently after changing severity.
Have each report apply its own copy of the severity matrix.

learningObjective: Choose how to keep itinerary travel time accurate when one leg is rebooked.

question.prompt: A rental itinerary stores travel legs in sequence. Its displayed travel time is the sum of each leg’s booked duration; waiting time is shown separately. Choose how to keep itinerary travel time accurate when one leg is rebooked.

options.text: Have RentalItinerary sum the booked durations of its current legs.
A canceled or replaced leg can be counted twice if a path misses the compensating update.
Derive a total from the member facts and exclude quantities the contract separates.

feedback.reason: Choose how to keep itinerary travel time accurate when one leg is rebooked. The prompt defines waiting time as a separate quantity, so that changes the meaning of travel time.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The prompt defines waiting time as a separate quantity, so that changes the meaning of travel time.
details.scenarioApplication: The itinerary owns the current legs and their booked durations.
details.errorCorrection: Let each booking screen add the new duration to a saved total when a leg changes. Include connection waiting time in each leg’s duration when rendering the itinerary.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Rebooking one leg changes the total once, while separately displayed waits remain outside it.
details.transfer: If the product later defines door-to-door journey time, add that as a distinct measure.

messages.text: Let each booking screen add the new duration to a saved total when a leg changes.
Include connection waiting time in each leg’s duration when rendering the itinerary.

learningObjective: Choose how the activation screen should display the deadline after a permitted edit.

question.prompt: A service window stores a start instant and an allowed duration. The deadline is start plus that duration; support staff may change either input before activation. Choose how the activation screen should display the deadline after a permitted edit.

options.text: The stored deadline can cease to match the two inputs the window says define it.
Calculate a deadline from its owned start and duration rather than maintaining a conflicting copy.
Have ServiceWindow calculate its deadline from its start and allowed duration.

feedback.reason: Choose how the activation screen should display the deadline after a permitted edit. A different screen may use another default and show another deadline.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A different screen may use another default and show another deadline.
details.scenarioApplication: ServiceWindow owns the inputs that define the deadline.
details.errorCorrection: Keep a deadline field that support must remember to update after changing the start. Have the activation screen independently add a default duration to the displayed start.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Changing a permitted input changes the displayed deadline through one rule.
details.transfer: Once activated, if the contract freezes the deadline, capture the resulting instant as an explicit lifecycle fact.

messages.text: Have the activation screen independently add a default duration to the displayed start.
Keep a deadline field that support must remember to update after changing the start.

learningObjective: Choose how to show proposed ingredient quantities without changing stored batch state.

question.prompt: A compost batch stores ingredient proportions and a target quantity. Operators can request a proposed batch size; the batch is not changed until the proposal is accepted. Choose how to show proposed ingredient quantities without changing stored batch state.

options.text: Use an operation that evaluates owned state while keeping a proposal distinct from an accepted transition.
Have CompostBatch calculate a proposal from its proportions and requested target without mutating itself.
That changes accepted state before the prompt’s explicit acceptance point.

feedback.reason: Choose how to show proposed ingredient quantities without changing stored batch state. The repeated calculation can use inconsistent proportions or rounding.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The repeated calculation can use inconsistent proportions or rounding.
details.scenarioApplication: The batch owns the proportions; a calculation can use them without committing a state change.
details.errorCorrection: Let the proposal screen overwrite the batch quantities while the operator is still reviewing. Have the operator copy each ingredient into a calculator and manually scale it.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The preview can be discarded safely or accepted later through its separate transition.
details.transfer: If proposals become independently saved records, model their own lifecycle rather than treating previews as accepted batches.

messages.text: Let the proposal screen overwrite the batch quantities while the operator is still reviewing.
Have the operator copy each ingredient into a calculator and manually scale it.

learningObjective: Choose how an existing case should continue to report its due instant after policy changes.

question.prompt: A support case stores its opened instant and response window. The due instant is fixed when the case is created; later policy edits affect new cases only. Choose how an existing case should continue to report its due instant after policy changes.

options.text: Have SupportCase retain and report the due instant calculated from its captured response window at creation.
That replaces the case’s stated captured deadline with a later policy value.
Keep lifecycle-captured state with the case whose history it defines.

feedback.reason: Choose how an existing case should continue to report its due instant after policy changes. Independent caches can disagree or be omitted by a new caller.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Independent caches can disagree or be omitted by a new caller.
details.scenarioApplication: The case owns the creation-time response window and the resulting deadline that governs its lifecycle.
details.errorCorrection: Recalculate the due instant from the policy currently published whenever a case is reopened. Ask every queue and notification caller to cache its own copy of the original deadline.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Policy changes apply to new cases while existing cases keep their original due instant.
details.transfer: A deliberate migration of open cases would be a separate explicit operation.

messages.text: Recalculate the due instant from the policy currently published whenever a case is reopened.
Ask every queue and notification caller to cache its own copy of the original deadline.

learningObjective: Choose how a new temperature reading should affect the zone’s heating state near the target.

question.prompt: A thermostat zone stores its target and current mode. Hysteresis keeps heating active until the measured temperature reaches the upper cutoff, rather than toggling at the target. Choose how a new temperature reading should affect the zone’s heating state near the target.

options.text: That discards the prior mode and can cause rapid toggling inside the hysteresis band.
Evaluate behavior from both the new input and the owner’s prior state when the rule is stateful.
Have ThermostatZone apply the reading using its target, mode, and hysteresis band.

feedback.reason: Choose how a new temperature reading should affect the zone’s heating state near the target. Multiple callbacks can disagree about the zone’s current mode and cutoff behavior.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Multiple callbacks can disagree about the zone’s current mode and cutoff behavior.
details.scenarioApplication: The zone owns the target and mode whose combination defines the next state.
details.errorCorrection: Have each sensor callback turn heating off whenever the reading reaches the target. Store the previous reading in each callback instance and let callbacks decide independently.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The same reading can produce different next states depending on whether the zone was already heating.
details.transfer: A sensor adapter can normalize units, but the zone still evaluates its state-dependent rule.

messages.text: Store the previous reading in each callback instance and let callbacks decide independently.
Have each sensor callback turn heating off whenever the reading reaches the target.

learningObjective: Choose how the preview should recalculate sheets after paper or duplex settings change.

question.prompt: A print job stores page count, paper size, and duplex setting. A fixed estimator maps those values to sheet count; users may change the settings before submission. Choose how the preview should recalculate sheets after paper or duplex settings change.

options.text: Keep a multi-input estimate aligned with the settings from which it is derived.
Have PrintJob calculate its estimated sheet count from its page count, paper size, and duplex setting.
A setting change can leave the estimate stale even though it is presented as current.

feedback.reason: Choose how the preview should recalculate sheets after paper or duplex settings change. They ignore the job’s selected paper or duplex state, so the number may not represent this job.

details.mechanismOrProperty: They ignore the job’s selected paper or duplex state, so the number may not represent this job.
details.scenarioApplication: PrintJob owns all three inputs that define the estimate.
details.errorCorrection: Let the preview store an independently editable sheet count next to the settings. Have printer drivers each estimate sheets from only page count.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Changing a setting updates the preview from the same calculation used by other consumers.
details.transfer: A device-specific physical estimate may be a separate collaborator if the prompt later adds device behavior.

messages.text: Let the preview store an independently editable sheet count next to the settings.
Have printer drivers each estimate sheets from only page count.
